title: Finite-presentation patching at a closed point with property detection
statement: Let $D$ be a Noetherian commutative ring (every ideal is finitely generated), $\mathfrak m$ a maximal ideal, $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$, $s\in S$ its closed point, $U=S\setminus\{s\}$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}D_{\mathfrak m}$ and $V=T\setminus\{\mathfrak mD_{\mathfrak m}\}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. For a scheme $Z$, let $\mathrm{FP}(Z)$ be the category of schemes of finite presentation over $Z$ and their $Z$-morphisms [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let $\mathcal P$ be the category of triples $(X_U,X_T,\alpha)$ with $X_U\in\mathrm{FP}(U)$, $X_T\in\mathrm{FP}(T)$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:X_U\times_UV\simeq X_T\times_TV$; its arrows are pairs of morphisms over $U$ and $T$ commuting with $\alpha$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The restriction functor $\mathrm{FP}(S)\to\mathcal P$ is an equivalence: every such triple is induced by an $S$-scheme of finite presentation, and every compatible pair of arrows between two restrictions lifts to a unique $S$-morphism. A scheme $X\in\mathrm{FP}(S)$ is smooth over $S$ if and only if $X_U$ and $X_T$ are smooth over their bases [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. It is separated over $S$ if and only if both restrictions are separated, where separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For a morphism $a:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FP}(S)$, $a$ is an open immersion if and only if $a_U$ and $a_T$ are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]; likewise $a$ is a closed immersion if and only if $a_U$ and $a_T$ are closed immersions.

source.place: Tag 0BPA (lemma-glueing-near-closed-point); property detection as in Tag 0EY3 (lemma-glueing-near-point-properties), using Tags 0C0C (lemma-descend-smooth), 01ZQ (lemma-descend-separated-finite-presentation), 0EUU (lemma-descend-open-immersion), 01ZP (lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation). Noetherian specialization ensures that arrows between the objects are locally of finite presentation.

proof.text: Use the directed set of affine open neighbourhoods $W$ of $s$, ordered by shrinking. Since $D$ is Noetherian, $S$ is locally Noetherian by its one affine chart, and is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the affine-scheme lemma. Thus $S$ is Noetherian. Every $W$ and $W\cap U$ is Noetherian by the open-subscheme lemma, and hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The local-ring canonical-morphism lemma identifies $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}$ with $T=\operatorname{Spec}D_{\mathfrak m}$. The affine-neighbourhood limit lemma gives $T=\varprojlim_W W$ with affine transitions. The only prime of $D_{\mathfrak m}$ contracting to $\mathfrak m$ is $\mathfrak mD_{\mathfrak m}$: such a prime contains this maximal ideal and hence equals it. Consequently $T\times_SU=V$. Apply the open-restriction clause of the affine-transition limit lemma to obtain $V=\varprojlim_W(W\cap U)$ with affine transitions; pullback by an open subscheme is the corresponding inverse-image open. All indexing sets here are sets of opens of the fixed space $S$, so they are small.

source.place: Tag 0BPA (lemma-glueing-near-closed-point), proof, the two neighbourhood limits; Tags 01YX and 01YW for limits and restriction to opens

proof.text: Given $(X_U,X_T,\alpha)$, apply clause (1) of finite-presentation spreading to $T=\varprojlim W$: choose $W_0$ and $X_0\to W_0$ of finite presentation with $(X_0)_T\simeq X_T$. For $W\subseteq W_0$, both $(X_U)_{W\cap U}$ and $(X_0)_{W\cap U}$ have finite presentation by base-change permanence. At the limit $V$, the given $\alpha$ and its inverse are arrows between these two fixed models. Apply clause (2) of spreading twice to the system $(W\cap U)$, then take a common smaller neighbourhood to obtain arrows $b$ and $c$ lifting $\alpha$ and $\alpha^{-1}$. Apply clause (3) to $cb$ and the identity, and to $bc$ and the identity. After a common further shrinking both identities hold. We have obtained an isomorphism $\beta:(X_U)_{W\cap U}\simeq(X_0)_ {W\cap U}$ whose restriction to $V$ is the prescribed $\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 0BPA, proof, finite-presentation descent on both limits; Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), clauses (1), (2), (3)

proof.text: Now $S=U\cup W$. Apply relative Zariski gluing to $X_U\to U$ and $X_W=(X_0)_W\to W$, with transition $\beta$ on $U\cap W$. For a two-member covering the self transitions are identities and the two distinct transitions are $\beta$ and $\beta^{-1}$, so the cocycle equations are exactly the inverse identities already imposed. The gluing lemma gives an $S$-scheme $X$ restricting to $X_U$ and $X_W$ compatibly with $\beta$. Its restriction to $T$ is $X_T$, because $T\to S$ factors through $W$; its induced overlap identification is the given $\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 0BPA, proof, first paragraph; constructions.tex, Relative glueing, Tag 01LG (section-relative-glueing)

proof.text: Check that this glued $X\to S$ has finite presentation, rather than only gluing its underlying schemes. The finite-presentation-at-a-point charts for $X_U\to U$ and $X_W\to W$ are also charts for $X\to S$: an affine open in either base open is an affine open in $S$. This gives local finite presentation by its definition, and, by the affine-open finite-presentation lemma, finite polynomial presentations on every affine chart; forgetting their relations gives local finite type. Since $U,W$ are quasi-compact and the two structure maps are quasi-compact, $X_U,X_W$ are quasi-compact by qcqs permanence. Their union $X$ is quasi-compact (combine finite subcovers on the two pieces), and the same permanence lemma makes $X\to S$ quasi-compact since $S$ is quasi-separated. Thus $X\to S$ is of finite type. The finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma makes $X$ Noetherian. In particular $X$ is quasi-separated, and qcqs permanence makes $X\to S$ quasi-separated. Together with local finite presentation this proves $X\in\mathrm{FP}(S)$. This proves essential surjectivity. Base-change permanence also ensures that restriction defines the stated functor on every object of $\mathrm{FP}(S)$.

source.place: Tag 0BPA, the restriction to schemes of finite presentation; properties.tex Tags 01OV and 01OY, morphisms.tex Tag 01T6; finite presentation is Definition 01TP

proof.text: For full faithfulness fix $X,Y\in\mathrm{FP}(S)$ and a compatible pair $a_U:X_U\to Y_U$, $a_T:X_T\to Y_T$. Restrict the fixed global models to the affine neighbourhoods $W$. Clause (2) of spreading over $T=\varprojlim W$ gives a lift $a_W:X_W\to Y_W$ of $a_T$ after shrinking $W$. On $W\cap U$ the arrows $a_W$ and $a_U$ have equal base change to $V$, by compatibility of the pair. Clause (3) of spreading over $V=\varprojlim(W\cap U)$ makes them equal after shrinking $W$ again. Their source and target models have finite presentation by base-change permanence. Glue $a_U$ and $a_W$ by the scheme-morphism gluing lemma. Their composites with $Y\to S$ equal $X\to S$ on this open covering, so uniqueness of gluing makes the resulting map an $S$-map. Its pullback to $T$ is $a_T$. Conversely, if two global $S$-maps have equal restrictions to $U$ and $T$, clause (3) for the system $W$ makes them equal on one smaller $W$, and they are equal on $U$ already. Uniqueness in morphism gluing makes them equal on $X$. Thus every compatible pair lifts to exactly one arrow, proving the claimed equivalence.

source.place: Tag 0BPA, final formal-combination sentence, expanded using Tag 01ZM (2),(3); schemes.tex Tag 01JA for morphism gluing

proof.text: For the detection clauses keep the same directed neighbourhood system and start from the fixed global finite-presentation schemes. The affine stages $W$ are qcqs, and $X_W,Y_W$ are qcqs by qcqs permanence. Their structure maps are locally of finite presentation. Any arrow $a:X\to Y$ over $S$ is locally of finite presentation by the over-base finite-presentation lemma: $X\to S$ is locally of finite presentation and $Y\to S$ is locally of finite type (forget the relations in its finite polynomial presentations). Its restrictions $a_W$ are locally of finite presentation by base-change permanence, and in particular locally of finite type. Thus the local-finite-presentation hypothesis for smooth/open-immersion descent and the local-finite-type hypothesis for closed-immersion descent are available. Separated descent needs no finiteness hypothesis on the arrow. None of these applications requires $X$ or $Y$ to be separated.

source.place: Tag 081D (situation-descent-property) and Tag 02FV (morphisms-lemma-finite-presentation-permanence); hypotheses for Tags 0C0C, 0EUU, 01ZP, 01ZQ

proof.text: Suppose $X_T\to T$ is smooth. Apply smooth descent to $X_W\to W$ and $T=\varprojlim W$ to obtain an affine neighbourhood $W$ over which $X_W\to W$ is smooth. If $X_U\to U$ is also smooth, the open-restriction smoothness lemma (its composition-with-the-base-open clause) makes $X_U\to S$ and $X_W\to S$ smooth. Smoothness on an open cover of the source then makes $X\to S$ smooth, as $X=X_U\cup X_W$. Conversely smooth base change gives smoothness of both $X_U\to U$ and $X_T\to T$.

source.place: Tag 0EY3, proof (1) with property smooth and Tag 0C0C; morphisms.tex Tags 01V6, 01VA, 01VC and 01VB

proof.text: Suppose $X_T\to T$ is separated. Apply separated descent to the structure morphisms $X_W\to W$, taking the target model to be $W$ itself, to get a neighbourhood $W$ with $X_W\to W$ separated. If $X_U\to U$ is separated too, the base-changed-diagonal criterion says that the restrictions of $\Delta:X\to X\times_SX$ over $U$ and $W$ are closed immersions. These are restrictions over the open cover $(X\times_SX)_U\cup(X\times_SX)_W=X\times_SX$. The closed-immersion target-locality lemma makes $\Delta$ a closed immersion, hence $X\to S$ separated. Conversely, if $\Delta$ is closed, its base changes along $U\to S$ and $T\to S$ are closed by closed-immersion base change; the same diagonal criterion gives separatedness of the two restrictions.

source.place: Tag 0EY3, proof (1), using Tag 01ZQ; locality of the closed diagonal and its base-change comparison

proof.text: Let $a:X\to Y$ be the arrow of the statement. If $a_T$ is an open immersion, apply open-immersion descent to the fixed arrows $a_W:X_W\to Y_W$ to obtain a neighbourhood $W$ on which $a_W$ is an open immersion. If instead $a_T$ is a closed immersion, apply closed-immersion descent to obtain $W$ on which $a_W$ is a closed immersion. The qcqs and local finite presentation/type hypotheses were verified in step 6. Thus in either case the local restriction on $T$ has been replaced by a restriction on an actual open neighbourhood $W$ of $s$.

source.place: Tag 0EY3, proof (2) with the two immersion properties, using Tags 0EUU and 01ZP

proof.text: The target opens $Y_U,Y_W$ cover $Y$, and their inverse images under the $S$-arrow $a$ are exactly $X_U,X_W$. If $a_U$ and $a_W$ are closed immersions, target locality of closed immersions therefore makes $a$ a closed immersion. Conversely both $a_U$ and $a_T$ are closed immersions when $a$ is one, by closed-immersion base change.

source.place: Tag 0EY3, proof (2), target-local assembly after Tag 01ZP

proof.text: If $a_U$ and $a_W$ are open immersions, their open images together form the image of $a$, which is open in $Y$. The map $a$ is injective: two points over the same $y$ both lie over any one of $Y_U,Y_W$ containing $y$, and the restriction there is injective. On these target opens $a$ has continuous inverse onto its image and induces an isomorphism of structure sheaves. The inverses and the sheaf isomorphisms agree on intersections because they are inverses to the same map. Hence $a$ is an isomorphism onto that open image, which is precisely the definition of open immersion. Conversely open-immersion base change gives both $a_U$ and $a_T$ when $a$ is an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 0EY3, proof (2), open-immersion assembly from its definition; schemes.tex Tag 01JY for base change

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BPA, proof, and Tag 0EY3, proof (1),(2), with smooth/open/closed descent supplied by Tags 0C0C, 0EUU and 01ZP and the formal combination written out.
